title: Neural-Behavioral Representation of Natural Whole-body Movement in Monkeys
claim: Raw multi-view recordings and neural signals are turned into skeletons, then decoded autoregressively through a pretrained behavior prior.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, setup then training/testing framework rows, autoregress loops
description: A wide two-panel figure. The left panel, titled 'System setup', shows a glass cage with a monkey, 8 wall-mounted cameras and x/y/z axes. A wireless router and a monitor sit below it. Beside the cage are three rows of camera-view photos, with the third row overlaid with skeleton keypoints. Below these are 3D skeleton renderings and wavy neural-signal traces, plus a skull diagram with electrode dots. A large grey arrow leads to the right panel, 'Computational framework'. That panel has two rows. The top row, 'Train behavior prior', shows the previous pose, current pose and neural signals feeding a grey trapezoid Encoder, a colored latent Gaussian blob, and a Decoder, which outputs the predicted pose. The bottom row, 'Decode skeleton movement', uses only the Decoder, with a frozen snowflake icon. Autoregress arrows loop back in both rows. Blue headings and flame/snowflake icons mark trainable and frozen modules.
caption: Pipeline for decoding natural whole-body movement from epidural neural signals. System setup: Whole-body movement data were captured using an 8-camera system and reconstructed into 3D skeleton. Synchronous recording of epidural neural signals from 62 channels were recorded and transmitted wirelessly. Computational framework: Collected data were divided into training and test sets. First, we trained a behavior prior on the training set by compressing movement data and neural signals into a latent space. Latent variables were then sampled and combined with the predicted state ˆpt−1 and the neural signals nt, and further passed through the decoder to reconstruct the current state ˆpt. During testing, only the decoder was used, and the movement states were reconstructed in the same autoregressive manner as during the training.
abstract: Understanding how cortical activity represents natural whole-body behaviors in primates remains challenging. Limited by the diversity of movements and inaccessibility of large-scale neural representation of whole-body kinematics, previous motor decoding studies focused on constrained tasks and limited limb movements. Here, we present a neural-behavioral recording and modeling framework for freely moving monkeys, combining large-scale epidural cortical signals from distributed sensory- and motor-related areas with synchronized multi-view motion capture through a custom-made data collection platform. We reconstructed whole-body monkey kinematics and learned a compact behavior prior using an autoregressive encoder-decoder model. Conditioned on neural signals, the model decoded accurate and realistic whole-body movement without explicit physical constraints. Our results provide a novel proof-of-concept approach for decoding natural whole-body movements in primates using large-scale intracranial neural activity.
